newsitem.title: USA: SPEED SKATING-XUE EDGES AILING SCHENK IN 500 METERS.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-XUE EDGES AILING SCHENK IN 500 METERS.

text.p: China's Ruihong Xue defeated an ailing Franziska Schenk in a 500 meters race on Saturday, but the German retained her lead in the World Cup speed skating standings.
Xue covered the distance on the the Pettit National Ice Centre oval in 39.77 seconds to beat Schenk, who clocked 39.90 for second place.
The difference was a fast start by Xue, who covered the first 100 meters in 10.64 seconds. Schenk's split time of 10.77 for the first 100 provided Xue with her margin of victory.
American Christine Witty finished tied for third in the 500 with Russian Svetlana Zhurova at 40.09 seconds and won the 1,000 meters in 1:20.19.
The victory moved Xue into second place in the World Cup 500-meter standings with 290 points, 10 behind Schenk.
Schenk also leads the 1,000-meter standings, despite pulling out of Saturday's race.
"I started having some problems with my stomach last week in Calgary," Schenk explained. "I still feel weak.
"Actually, I'm pretty proud of myself for finishing second in the 500 today, considering how badly I felt."
Manabu Horii of Japan maintained his lead in the men's standings over both sprint distances with a victory in the 1,000 meters and a third-place at 500.
Grunde Njos of Norway won the 500 in 36.62 seconds, with American Casey Fitzrandolph taking second.
Horii's clocked 1:12.99 to win the 1,000 with Jan Bos of the Netherlands second in 1:13.24 and Fitzrandolph third.
